A vendor who owns or is responsible for one or more subsidiary vendors, e.g. headquarters vendor with one or more branches or divisions. Multiple layers of parent/subsidiary relationships are possible. Many Pay To Vendors will not have a "Parent Pay To Vendor“
A Vendor Pay To is an entity to whom remittance is made. Vendor Pay To is called Supplier in Oracle Accounts Payable.
This is the entity we actually pay hence the name "Pay To"

A Vendor Order From is a merchant-defined merchandise grouping that constitutes the level which supports the ordering and management of goods. This grouping may or may not represent a legal company. The corresponding Vendor Pay To can differ from this vendor.
This is the entity that we submit Purchase Order's to and associate with items hence the name "Order From"
A trade-marked image developed by a designer/manufacturer to convey the design concepts and quality characterizing the products carrying the brand, e.g.
, Ralph Lauren.  A brand may include one or more labels, one of which may have an identical name to that of the brand.
This is typically the customer facing name

A name used to group merchandise styles, defined by the designer and identified by a label sewn into the garment or a logo displayed on the merchandise.  A branded label (sub-brand) may have a name identical to, or a derivative of, the parent brand to evoke the associated emotion

A grouping of third party Vendor Partners which are defined by categories such as raw materials, finished products or services. These partners (brokers, agents, ticket partners, etc.) assist in getting product to its final destination, i.e. the retail store. A vendor partner may or may not be a financial entity.

New, critical JWN initiatives1 have highlighted how JWN has an increasingly complex and siloed approach to vendor management (VM). We require brands to work with and across many teams2 and tools3 to build, manage and grow their business with us. 

The feedback is clear: we are more difficult to work with than many of our competitors who have taken action to make vendor interactions frictionless. Our current setup isn’t working for our vendors, our teams, or for JWN. We believe we need to act now – especially as we grow via Unowned Inventory – to continue to be/become the retailer of choice for the world’s best brands.

3 JWN tools (example only): Supplier portal, NuOrder, Retail Hub, Email
